body: I was prepared to be disappointed having lost Dame Maggie Smith. My to my surprise, the rest of the cast was able to carry off sound performances, ESPECIALLY Michelle Dockery who clearly was Grandmama's favorite, and mine! She has spent years developing and evolving the Charactor or Mary. Once again, she takes us along with her to the next evolution of Mary without disconnecting her past. This is the result of good writing, but more importantly, an exceptional performance. Writers cleverly shifted much of Lady Grantham's quips and persona to Mary, which follows the notion that Mary is becoming what Grandmama Grantham was, a pioneer in a new era while retaining the best of what was in the past. Home Run for Michelle Dockery. The screenplay was logical and flowed well. So happy to see another favorite, Thomas, back and giving us closure to another pivitol charactor. No spoilers here, but fans will be happy. I especially enjoyed the added attention the writers gave the Elizabeth McGovern's charactor, and she made the very best of that opportunity. Bring some tissues for the final scene. Downton Abby fans will not be disappointed and new fans will be compelled to step back in time to the beginning of the series and two previous movies. A BIG THANK YOU TO THE ENTIRE CAST.

When Mary finds herself in a public scandal and the family faces financial trouble, the household grapples with the threat of social disgrace. The Crawleys must embrace change with the next generation leading Downton Abbey into the future.

Honestly, my watched every episode and I paid enough attention to follow along. These characters are all so well written that they really do feel like a family, your family. From the actual family to the servants of the house, you care about each and everyone.

This film is a beautiful send off to a wonderful series. Yes, I think anybody who has watched the show knows this ending has been coming almost since the first episode. The "twist" in this movie is obvious and not shocking come time for reveal. However, that really takes a backseat to the emotion that comes with this project. I was never a die hard watcher and even I got a little emotional at the end. I can only imagine how true fans must feel. It's a pity that more shows can't end with this satisfying of a finale.

IMDb gives it a 7.7/10 For me, it's a 7.5/10

Right or wrong, weak or strong...these are my opinions.

What a gift Julian Fellowes has been. Creating a world that so many can relate to and genuinely feel as if they are part of it, though only observers. Having watched from the beginning 14 years ago, waiting patiently for the next episode then movie, it astounds me how emotionally invested I've been. Many viewings have touched me, connected with me. The writing here has delivered an "ending" that completes the story, wraps up the story, ends the story competently and efficiently. But even in its efficient spareness, if you have been a follower or not, it will still deeply affect you. Succumb to it, and hope that other writers learn from it, because this is how films are meant to be written. Thank you Mr Fellowes.

As a long-time fan of the series, I found the Downton Abbey farewell film truly moving. It brought together all of main characters for a final glimpse into their lives through 1930, blending heartfelt moments with just the right touch of humor. The film beautifully pays tribute to the show's legacy and brings out the strengths of each character as they adapt to a new era. It offers a satisfying closure that resonated deeply with me-so much so that I cried at the end as if saying goodbye to beloved friends. I appreciate the care taken to wrap up the story for loyal viewers. Thank you to everyone involved in creating this touching farewell.

I'm glad I went to see it. Understandably, the film is constructed to please long time Downton fans. There is a rather self-conscious effort to give some characters enough screen time to bid us farewell, so that we see Anna and Mr Bates or Mrs Patmore and Daisy in brief scenes not at all relevant to the story at hand. That's fine, but I can almost imagine a producer standing behind the camera with a stopwatch to check off a box (okay Mrs Crawley, we've reached your quota).

Even the gone and departed appear briefly-Maggie Smith, Matthew, and one delicious shot of Sybil. Gee I wish she hadn't left the show. The storyline itself, emphasized in the trailer as a big scandal involving Mary, doesn't have a lot of punch to be honest, but I guess that's not why Downton fans are here anyway. For my money the worthwhile themes are a softening of class structure (Robert asking Carson for advice) and the virtual end of a centuries-long servant culture in Britain.
